title: Introduce Idempotency-Cookie and normalized error envelope for graceful stream fallbacks
author: Maya Patel
body:
Context and motivation: Customers integrating streamed tool/function outputs reported two recurring failure modes: 1) opaque stream failures with inconsistent retry guidance, and 2) difficulty reconciling idempotency across multiplexed HTTP/2 and SSE sessions. This made it hard for language agents to reliably retry or resume work without risking duplicate tool-effects. Goal: provide a small surface that (a) gives clients a stable, machine-readable error envelope at stream end-frames, (b) surfaces a lightweight session-level idempotency artifact that survives reconnects (Idempotency-Cookie), and (c) map legacy OpenAI-style HTTP errors into the same envelope so the OpenAI shim gets predictable semantics.

What this PR does (high level): Introduces an "Idempotency-Cookie" header and server-side cookie token emitted on stream start; implements a normalized error envelope emitted as a final control frame (type: "error_envelope") for all stream terminations that are not clean 200/OK end-of-streams; extends the OpenAI compatibility adapter to translate 4xx/5xx responses into the same envelope; and adds conservative retry/reconnect hooks in the router to prefer session-resume when the Idempotency-Cookie is present. The change intentionally keeps ephemeral tokens opaque to clients — they can send back the cookie on reconnect but cannot parse its internals.

Compatibility and contract: The error envelope is a JSON object with fields: code (string), message (string), retry_after (milliseconds or null), scope (string: 'session'|'request'), and hint (optional string). For streaming transports that don't support explicit end frames, the adapter will send a final chunk prefixed with "__RW_ERR__" followed by the envelope JSON to preserve compatibility. Existing clients that ignore the envelope will see a normal stream close; well-behaved clients should parse the envelope and act on retry_after and scope.

Key implementation notes: - Added server/streaming/idempotency_cookie.go: generates short-lived opaque tokens, stores mapping in in-memory session store with optional Redis backing controlled by configuration. - Added server/streaming/error_envelope.go: canonical error envelope builder and serializer, plus streaming-framing helper for transports (SSE, chunked, HTTP/2). - Router changes (server/router/streaming_router.go): on transient failures, if Idempotency-Cookie present and session state compatible, respond with 409 + envelope with scope=session and retry_after hint; if not present, return 429/503 mapping depending on upstream hint. - OpenAI adapter updates (openai/adapter/stream_shim.go): translate legacy Retry-After and X-RateLimit-* headers into retry_after in envelope; map model-specific transient codes into canonical codes ("rate_limit", "server_unavailable", "kv_cache_miss"). - SDK updates: added lightweight parser helpers in redwood-sdk-python and redwood-sdk-typescript to extract Idempotency-Cookie and envelope when present.

Testing and validation: Added unit tests for envelope serialization and parsing (tests/streaming/error_envelope_test.go), integration tests that simulate reconnect/resume flows against a fake backend (tests/streaming/idempotency_cookie_integration_test.go), and end-to-end smoke tests against the OpenAI shim to ensure header->envelope mapping. CI: lint, unit, integration, and canary benchting were run. Observability: new metrics: streaming.error_envelope.emitted, streaming.idempotency_resume.success, streaming.idempotency_resume.conflict.

Rollback and feature toggles: Feature guarded behind config flag `features.streaming_idempotency_cookie` (off by default for on-prem until Redis session-backed store is enabled). Backwards compatibility: default behavior for clients remains unchanged (streams close as before); envelope is additive. Operators can opt-out by disabling the feature flag.

Checklist: - [x] Implemented token generator + in-memory store with Redis option - [x] Implemented envelope framing for SSE/HTTP chunked/H2 - [x] Adapter mappings for OpenAI shim - [x] Tests: unit + integration + e2e smoke - [x] Docs: added docs/api/streaming-error-envelope.md and examples in quickstarts - [x] Benchmarked overhead (0.4% median p99 token latency increase under synthetic load) - [x] Security review pass (cookie is opaque, signed, short TTL)

Release notes: Adds Idempotency-Cookie header for session resume and a normalized streaming error envelope that provides retry_after and canonical error codes. Default behavior unchanged for clients that do not parse the envelope. See docs/api/streaming-error-envelope.md for migration guidance.

b2c3d4e: implement error envelope framing and serializer
c3d4e5f: wire envelope into streaming runtime and adapters
d4e5f6a: update openai shim header mapping and tests
e5f6a7b: add SDK helper parsers and examples
f6a7b8c: add docs and feature flag gating
g7b8c9d: fix race in session resume path after reviewer feedback
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can we avoid storing full session state in memory for hosted tier? Suggest pluggable Redis and bounded LRU fallback.
Maya Patel: Implemented pluggable store with Redis-backed config and an in-memory LRU fallback; documented TTL and eviction behaviour.
Ruth Chen: The 409 vs 429 semantics were unclear. Recommend explicit mapping in the router.
Maya Patel: Clarified router logic: 409 used when resume conflict detected with existing session, 429 used for rate limit with retry_after present, 503 for backend transient failures. Added tests.
Diego Alvarez: Need to ensure OpenAI shim mapping doesn't expose internal error codes. Suggest whitelist.
Maya Patel: Added canonical code whitelist and mapping table; shim emits only canonical codes and a human hint.
Liam O'Connor: Approve after minor comment about metric naming
release_notes: Adds an opaque Idempotency-Cookie for stream session resumption and a normalized streaming error envelope (code, message, retry_after, scope). OpenAI adapter maps legacy headers into the envelope. Feature is behind a config flag for gradual rollout.
